decisions.fork: F1 Intervention: how the forecast is built and how H is chosen
decisions.choice: Make the PRIMARY intervention a promise-layer ('display') correction, scored by exact offline replay of the recorded runs. Use the dispatch-integrated v1.3 wrapper only for the secondary question of whether the deadline rule is rescued. Forecast: a 15-min citywide profile m(b), the equal-weight mean of the measured factor over PRIOR same-kind days in the data week. This is causal: 14/11 uses 12-13, 15/11 uses 12-14, 16/11 uses 12-15, 18/11 uses 17, and 17/11 has no forecast, so it stays naive. Anchor multiplicatively on the current measured bin (ratio m(tau)/m(t)). Hold the profile constant after bin 8, exactly as the world does. One-sided rule: the promise is never shortened, P' = max(P_naive, P_fc). Display layer: stretch each rider's own horizon D = P0 - t0 through the forecast path, which needs no H. v1.3: r(t) = max(1, mean over [t, t+H] of m(tau)/m(t)), recomputed at each bin refresh. H = 900 s is fixed a priori as the median first-drop horizon on dev runs (727-799 s), rounded up to the 15-min bin. H is never tuned. Pre-declared sensitivities, which are not decision rules: leave-one-out same-kind pool, a pool excluding 12/11 and 15/11, and a two-sided forecast.
decisions.rationale: (1) In this world the rider's arrival time is a deterministic function of the first promise and the citywide factor path. For riders whose dispatch part is zero, actual alight minus a promise stretched by the true factor path lies in [-1.3, 0] s. So the promise-side benefit of a forecast can be computed exactly with zero runs. Simulating it would measure a closed-form consequence of the factor files, which is circular. (2) The uniform r(t) that v1.3 needs, because the Runner snapshot is static, approximates worse than the per-trip stretch. On calibration 07-09: uniform H=15 gives 3.03% late, the per-trip forecast 0.93%. (3) A two-sided forecast hurts 17-19 (calibration: late >60 s goes from 0.00% to 1.27%, early >60 s from 0.26% to 1.03%). The one-sided rule gives 0.00% in every 17-19 calibration cell, and it matches the asymmetric loss in the business sources (lateness hurts more than earliness helps). (4) Leave-one-out uses future days, and a reviewer would call that leakage. The causal pool did as well on calibration cells (e.g. 14/11 r2 07-09: causal 0.00% vs leave-one-out 3.70%). (5) The world holds the factor after the window ends, so a forecast that does not hold would carry artificial error.

decisions.fork: F4 Primary outcomes and decision rules
decisions.choice: Per served rider: t0 = publishedAtMs of the drop initialPromise; P0 = its p; A = simTimeMs of the passengerAlighted batch. P_F1 = max(P0, t0 + Stretch(t0, P0 - t0; causal profile)). L60_c = share of served riders in cell c with A - P > 60 s. Arm value = unweighted mean over cells, as in T3.8; the rider-pooled value is a sensitivity. E60_c = share with A - P < -60 s. Ext_c = mean(P_F1 - P0). Equal-price pad: P_pad = P0 + k(P0 - t0), with k = sum(P_F1 - P0)/sum(P0 - t0) over all test C-30 riders, computed from promises only and blind to A. PRIMARY family (Holm, α = 0.05; cluster bootstrap over the 13 day-windows; B = 10,000; fixed seed; cell bootstrap also reported for comparability). H-F1 (C-30, 34 cells): passes if the upper bound of ΔL60 (F1 - naive) < -1.0 pp, AND (point estimates) Ext ≤ 45 s, AND ΔE60 ≤ +1.0 pp. H-F2: passes if the upper bound of L60(F1) - L60(pad) < 0, which is the 'forecast beats equal-price padding' test. SECONDARY. H-F3 (Mplus-30-F vs Mplus-30, 19 cells, 7 day-window clusters): the own-promise break share (A > the arm's first promise + 30 s) AND the forced-decision share each fall by ≥ 50% relative (point), with the 95% upper bound of the absolute difference < 0. Service non-inferiority: the 95% lower bound of the served difference > -2 riders per cell. H-F4 (C-30-F vs C-30, 19 cells): the same non-inferiority margin of -2 per cell, plus the H2a replication |C-F - M+-F served| ≤ 2 per cell. Windows are descriptive. 07-09 is pre-declared as where the mechanism should show; there are no per-window pass rules.
decisions.rationale: The display layer leaves dispatch untouched, so the comparison is paired at the RIDER level with an identical served set. That removes the confound of changed served sets for the primary claim. The equal-price pad comparator answers the obvious attack, 'you just promised later'. On dev the pad already removes much of the lateness (task B 7.25% to 1.80%; calibration 17.66% to 5.56%), so H-F2 is a real test, not a formality. The -2 riders per cell margin reuses the T3.9 H2a margin. The 45 s price ceiling is a judgment fixed before seeing outcomes. It is about 5% of the published mean door-to-door time of 861 s; that this is a tolerable price is unverified. Clustering by day-window reflects the shared factor path. The cell-level bootstrap is kept only for comparability with the T3.8 report.

decisions.fork: F7 Threats to validity and mitigations
decisions.choice: Ten threats, each with a mitigation. (1) Uniform citywide factor: lateness is deterministic in the factor path, so the forecast benefit is close to a tautology. Mitigation: say so explicitly; frame it as the measured share of real rush-hour growth that is anticipable, passed through real promise horizons; run the per-edge-noise robustness test; make no claim about real-world size. (2) Temporal leakage from leave-one-out. Mitigation: the causal pool is primary. (3) Thin, unusual history: only 12-18/11 have 15-min factors; 12/11 is a Monday, probably the observed Veterans Day holiday (unverified; consistent with its 08:00 factor of 2.797 vs 3.34-3.54 on 13-15/11); 15/11 is the storm afternoon; the weekend pool is a single day. Mitigation: pre-declared pool sensitivities; describe the result as a lower bound on what months of history would give (unverified). (4) Clustering. Mitigation: cluster by day-window and report counts (07-09 test = 4 mornings). (5) Reusing T3.8 test cells: the naive lateness by window is already published, but the forecast-adjusted outcomes have not been computed on test. Mitigation: freeze the method on dev, seal, then compute on test once. Disclose that the one-sided and causal choices came from today's dev exploration. (6) Changed served sets in the F arms. Mitigation: the primary claim comes from the display layer with identical riders; the F arms get full-demand metrics plus a common-rider analysis. (7) Snowstorm. Its demand is completed TLC trips, but each cell still draws 108 requests (eligible 1,508-2,257 vs about 2,500-3,100 on normal days), so the demand collapse is NOT simulated. The fixture base is the 00:00 factor and the world applies only the ratio within the window, so the storm's absolute level (1.36-2.17× other weekdays) is absent. Two overlapping windows from one afternoon. Mitigation: descriptive only. (8) Scale: under the capped rules, late > 300 s is 0, while contracts trigger at 10-15 min. Mitigation: state that the benefit is reliability of the shown time, not avoided penalties. (9) The display layer assumes riders do not react, since the sim has no cancellations. It also creates a ledger mismatch: the C ledger records Runner promises, not displayed ones. Mitigation: state both; the F arms show the integrated alternative. (10) Implementation of v1.3 (snapshot patch, ms rounding, dirty-flag timing). Mitigation: forecast-off and identity-forecast equivalence controls, with a halt rule.
decisions.rationale: These are the attacks a reviewer would most likely use to demolish the result. Each mitigation either removes the confound or narrows the claim to what the data can carry.

decisions.fork: F8 Direction check: is forecast-aware promising the best use of ~5 weeks and ~110 runs?
decisions.choice: Yes, but only in re-scoped form, not as the 5-arm v1.3 programme. As planned, 5 arms × 34 cells = 170 runs exceeds the budget. Worse, it would spend runs measuring a deterministic consequence of the factor files. Recommended: (i) a zero-run promise-layer forecast plus the three-way attribution on all existing test runs; this is the practical, UX-facing result the advisor asked for: reliable shown times and an accountability split. (ii) About 71 runs for what only simulation can answer: whether forecast-aware first promises rescue the deadline rule (a fairness check on T3.9's central C-vs-M+ claim), the served price of integration, real snowstorm stress, and robustness to traffic that cannot be forecast. (iii) Protect writing time, because the thesis and docs/18/19 still do not include T3.8/T3.9 (handoff memory). Alternatives rejected: the full 170-run matrix (over budget and circular); tuning H over 3 values on dev (24+ runs for a parameter the primary analysis does not need); more T3.8-style cells (no further days with 15-min factors); dropping the forecast entirely (a reviewer will raise the M+ artefact question anyway).
decisions.rationale: Research value: a falsifiable mechanism claim (lateness under C is entirely traffic, and the anticipable part can be removed at a measured price) and a fairness test of the thesis's own headline contrast, which may weaken it; that must be reported either way. Practical value: a deployable correction that leaves the dispatcher untouched, matching how ETA layers are used in industry (Uber DeepETA, cited in ADR-075). Its price in seconds is measured, and it lines up with the 'not anticipated at scheduling' test in the paratransit rules. No novelty claim, since time-of-day forecasting is standard. The contribution is the measured effects plus the attribution tool.

decisions.fork: F1 Intervention: how the forecast is built and how H is chosen
decisions.choice: Anchored, per-bin, floored growth forecast with a fixed H = 30 min that is never tuned. At each 15-min bin start t_b, the Runner's snapshot = the measured current-bin arc (same as v1.2) x r_b, with r_b = max(1, mean over [t_b, t_b+30 min] of m(tau)/m(t_b)). Because m is a 15-min step function, this reduces to r_b = max(1, (m_b + m_{b+1}) / (2 m_b)), i.e. half the next 15-min step, never shortening. m = mean 15-min factor of the OTHER weekdays among 12-16/11 (leave-one-out), read only inside [windowStart, windowStart+7200] and holding the last value, exactly as the world does. Weekends get r_b = 1, by a minimum-history rule of at least 3 source days. FleetPy keeps driving measured times. H comes from an a priori lead-time rule: H = 2 x (mean offset into the bin of 7.5 min + mean promise-to-drop lead time / 2). Dev C-30 lead time is about 727 s, which gives about 27 min, rounded to 30 min.
decisions.rationale: Anchoring on the current measured level is essential: the world is anchored at the window start, and on the snow day an absolute historical level would be badly wrong. Only relative growth is forecast, so the forecast inherits the current level and cannot see a snowstorm coming, which is the honest behaviour. Updating once per bin keeps promise revisions at bin boundaries only, as in v1.2, so no extra visible jitter. The floor rests on evidence that lateness costs more than earliness (Harter 2025, Mao 2025 in SOURCES) and on dev evidence: without the floor, weekend w17 dev lateness went from 0 to 1.9%. Weekends have only one source day, which does not make a profile. Dev checks show H = 30 per-bin gives 0 early arrivals > 60 s, while H = 45 overshoots (5.2% early > 60 s). A definitional trap: if the per-bin step version used H = 15 min, then r would be exactly 1 and the intervention would do nothing.

decisions.fork: F1 Intervention: how the forecast is built and how H is chosen
decisions.choice: Use the existing v1.3 wrapper unchanged (forecast-v1). The Runner's snapshot is the measured current-bin arc × r_b, with r_b = (1/K)·Σ_{j<K} m(b+j)/m(b). It is anchored on the current measured level: only the growth shape comes from other days, never their absolute level. r is piecewise-constant per 15-min bin, and r = 1 from bin 8 on, matching the world's hold. K = 2 (H = 30 min) is fixed before sealing. Source days: leave-one-day-out over the other same-kind days of 12–18/11, always excluding 15/11 (the documented snowstorm day) and the scenario day. Weekdays use the other weekdays minus 15/11; weekends use the other weekend day. Aggregator: the implemented mean of absolute profiles. No clamp in the primary arm. No tuning by simulation, and no test-cell information is used. Sensitivities run on display-only quotes with zero runs: past-only (causal) sources, a one-sided clamp r = max(1, r), and K = 3.
decisions.rationale: Anchoring cancels day-level differences (for example 16/11 and 12/11 run much lower than 13–14/11) and keeps the method valid on incident days. Excluding 15/11 follows the regulatory meaning of 'anticipated' (regular patterns), not an outcome. On test days it changes r by ≤ 0.003. K = 2 is derived in advance: the promise horizon is about 13 min (median), and r is refreshed only at bin starts, so the expected share of travel in the next bin is about 0.45 (r ≈ 1 + ½(g − 1)). Dev data corroborate it under a padding-proof criterion: MAE of first-drop-promise error is a proper score for the median, and K = 2 minimises it in all three dev configurations. Larger K lowers the late share only by over-padding (negative bias, rising MAE), which would be gaming. Keeping the symmetric forecast primary avoids a code change and an extra dev-selected fork. It also exposes the real harm in falling-traffic windows; the clamp is reported as a zero-run deployment option.

decisions.fork: F4 Primary outcomes and decision rules
decisions.choice: Definitions follow t38_rider_experience.py. A_r = first passengerAlighted simTime − drop ETA of the rider's initialPromise ledger entry. Cell metric L_j = share of served riders with A_r > 60 s (unweighted cell mean over 34 cells). served_j = completed riders. Inference: paired cell bootstrap, B = 10,000, new sealed seed, 95% percentile interval (sorted index 249/9750). Resampling is stratified by window (9/14/11) as primary; unstratified is a sensitivity that keeps continuity with T3.9. The three hypotheses below form a fixed-sequence gatekeeping family (each at two-sided 95%; FWER ≤ 0.05). H-F1 (closed loop, superiority): Δ = L(C-30F) − L(C-30); pass iff UB95 < 0 AND point estimate ≤ −1.0 pp (minimum meaningful effect, about 24% of the 4.12% baseline). H-F2 (service non-inferiority), tested only if H-F1 passes: served(C-30F) − served(C-30); pass iff LB95 ≥ −2 riders per cell (the T3.9 margin). H-F3 (information beats padding), tested only if H-F1 and H-F2 pass: display-only quote layer on the 34 naive C-30 test runs, applied after the seal. Compare late60 under the forecast quote t0 + r_b·(p − t0) against a constant multiplicative pad κ, with κ solved so the pad's cell-mean ABSOLUTE extension equals the forecast's (generous to padding); pass iff UB95 < 0. Claim 'forecast-aware promising is beneficial' iff H-F1 ∧ H-F2 (intersection–union test, no adjustment needed). Claim '…because of time-of-day information, not padding' only if H-F3 also passes. Pre-declared downgrade rules: if the estimate on the common-served set has UB ≥ 0, label the claim 'not robust to served-set change'; if any leave-one-day-out estimate is ≥ 0, label it 'driven by one day'. Windows, snow and all other outcomes are descriptive, reported with CIs, without significance language.
decisions.rationale: Late > 60 s against the first promise is the rider- and contract-facing metric already used in T3.8. It can be gamed by padding and by rejecting hard riders, so H-F3 (padding-proof, exactly paired on identical riders, zero runs) and H-F2 plus the common-set check close both loopholes. Stratification matches the fixed design (window counts were set by the normaliser, not sampled). Cells share day-level traffic, hence the leave-one-day-out check. The fixed sequence avoids Bonferroni loss while controlling the family. Power (rough, assumed noise): with per-cell effect −θ·L_j(C-30) plus N(0, σ) noise, θ = 0.5 gives mean −2.06 pp and P(UB < 0) ≈ 0.98–1.00 for σ ∈ {0.01, 0.02}. θ = 0.25 gives −1.03 pp and 0.98/0.69, and then the −1 pp minimum effect would fail about half the time. σ is unverified.

decisions.choice: All are paired, descriptive, with 95% stratified bootstrap CIs. (1) Price riders see: cell-mean change in quoted door-to-door (first drop ETA − request time) and in quoted wait (first pickup ETA − request), C-30F − C-30, plus p50/p90 of the per-rider extension on common riders. (2) Accuracy: MAE and signed bias of A; late > 120 s and > 300 s; late pickup > 60 s. (3) Service and experience: served share, wait mean/p90, ride, door-to-door, on-time-served per request (= served ∧ A ≤ 60 s, over 108), which cannot be gamed by rejection. (4) Promise stability: visible60/visible120 (E2), jump share, S_j = max_r Σ|x|, and the share of test cells with S_j ≤ 222.259 s under C-30F. No γ recalibration (it would need 15 runs and is out of scope). (5) Rules: C-30F non-normal decisions; Mplus-30F vs Mplus-30 forced share and own-promise broken (A > 30 s); C-30F vs Mplus-30F served difference (H2a replication, ±2) and action-sequence agreement. (6) Attribution under C-30F: A^F = Σc (dispatch) + Σx (unanticipated revisions) + residual (forecast error at execution; no longer 0 under v1.3). The anticipated part relative to the naive promise is ≈ (1 − 1/r_b0)(p0 − t0), approximate because dwell is also scaled. Report shares among late riders: what is excusable as unanticipated vs the operator's part. (7) Zero-run quote-layer extras: padding frontier κ ∈ {0, 0.5, …, 6}% with the closed-loop C-30F point overlaid; clamp variant; past-only sources; per-window conformal additive buffer (90th percentile of A on calibration cells). (8) Validity checks: '[world]' lines identical between arms per cell; r-lines equal to the sealed r-table. (9) Business translation, labelled ILLUSTRATIVE: late riders per 1,000 × $5 (Via) / $10 (A-A-R), and the demand effect of the longer quoted wait at elasticity −0.0427.
decisions.rationale: The advisor asked for UX and business value, so the price (longer quotes) must sit next to the punctuality gain. The rejection-proof composite and the common-set view address selection. S_j and visible changes test whether anticipating growth reduces promise churn; the mechanism is ambiguous (within-bin early arrivals may add small negative revisions), so no directional claim. Attribution maps directly onto 49 CFR 37.131(f)(3)(ii). The money figures are illustrative because the field thresholds are minutes, not 60 s.

decisions.fork: F7 Threats to validity and mitigations
decisions.choice: (1) A uniform citywide factor makes forecasting easy and scaling path-neutral. Mitigation: no real-world effect-size claim; frame the result as an upper bound for this forecast class; report factor-level forecast error. (2) Source days include future days of the same week (non-causal); 12/11 may be a holiday (unverified). Mitigation: zero-run past-only sensitivity, which was close on calibration (MAE 12.8 vs 13.2 s) but weaker on task-B. (3) Reuse of T3.8 test cells whose naive outcomes are known. Mitigation: all 34 cells; K fixed from dev data; no forecast-on computation of any kind on test cells before the seal; disclose every pre-seal look (factor accuracy on all days, dev quote layer, determinism check). (4) Calibration cells share days with test cells. Mitigation: K corroborated on the day-disjoint task-B set. (5) Changed served sets (selection). Mitigation: H-F2, common-set downgrade rule, rejection-proof composite. (6) Padding confound. Mitigation: H-F3 and the padding frontier. (7) Cells within a day are correlated. Mitigation: leave-one-day-out rule; stratified bootstrap. (8) Display-only approximation (dwell scaled). Mitigation: used only for H-F3 and sensitivities, where both quote rules share the approximation; closed loop stays primary. (9) Snow: completed-trip demand (survivorship); 108 requests per cell fixed; time-of-day confound (14–17h vs test windows); partial cell build. Mitigation: descriptive only; cite flat normal-afternoon factor profiles and the w17 analogue instead of claiming causality. (10) Scale gap: 60-s lateness vs the minute-scale harms in the field data. Mitigation: label money as illustrative; report late > 300 s. (11) Implementation and comparator errors. Mitigation: unit tests and mutants, sham control, positive control, r-table manipulation check, independent re-analysis agent from raw transcripts as in T3.8, reviewer agent tracing every number to a saved output. (12) Disk truncation. Mitigation: pre-declared priority order and a seeded-random order within tiers, so any truncation leaves a random subset.
decisions.rationale: Each listed threat could otherwise be used to attribute the result to tuning, selection, leakage or artefact. Each mitigation is either a pre-declared rule or a zero-run analysis, so the run budget is preserved.

decisions.choice: Proceed with forecast-aware promising. risks: Disk: if the policy floors are GiB (as Windows shows them), the real budget is about 85–93 runs, not ~110. Tier C (Mplus-30F test) could be truncated; the seeded-random order keeps any truncation unbiased, but power drops.

The closed-loop effect may be smaller than the display-only dev estimate (dwell is not scaled in the snapshot; inflated travel times change dispatch). H-F1 could then pass on UB < 0 but miss the −1.0 pp minimum meaningful effect. Per the rough power estimate this is likely if the true relative reduction is about 25%.

Service non-inferiority (H-F2) could fail in w07: r up to about 1.06 tightens the 600 s pickup windows and maxRideTime feasibility, so the Runner rejects more requests. I rate this medium-low confidence.

Mechanism risk for promise stability: under v1.3, vehicles move at measured speed while the Runner expects r × measured, so within-bin early arrivals can create extra small revisions. visible60 and S_j may worsen. No directional prediction was sealed.

Forecasting a decline in w17 (r < 1) will likely create some lateness where C-30 currently has none (dev: 0% → 0.77%). This must be reported as a real harm; the clamp is only a zero-run, exploratory remedy.
Mplus-30F may close much of the forced-share and broken-promise gap with C-30. That would weaken the thesis's practical distinction of C over Mplus, and it must be reported honestly.

External validity: a uniform citywide factor makes forecasting easy and leaves shortest paths unchanged, so the effect is an upper bound for this forecast class. The source days include future days of the same week; 12/11 may be a holiday (unverified).

The snow set is incomplete (5/8 cells built, 3 pending). It uses completed-trip demand and is confounded with time of day (14–17h), so it supports descriptive stress statements only, not causal claims.
Business value: the documented field harms start at minutes (Via 10 min; A-A-R ≥ 15 min past the window), while the primary metric is 60 s. Money translations are illustrative only.

Every exploratory number in this design (K-selection MAEs, dev late shares, matched-padding results, the determinism check, the power estimate) was computed read-only in this session and NOT saved. Each must be regenerated by a saved script with an output file before the plan cites it or is sealed.

The equivalence comparator must ignore run-salted fields (runId, publicationId(s), *Hash). A comparator that is too lenient could hide a real difference, so it needs the positive control (U vs C-30 must differ) and a mutation test before use.

revisedDecisions.fork: F1 Intervention: forecast construction and H
revisedDecisions.choice: PRIMARY is a promise-layer (display) forecast with a time-dependent per-trip stretch. It is scored exactly by offline replay of the existing runs. For each published ETA p at time t, show d = max(p, t + S(t, p - t)). S runs the rider's remaining horizon at the current measured level until the end of the current 15-min bin, then at the current level x m̂(b)/m̂(b_t), holding from bin 8 as the world does. m̂ is the mean measured 15-min factor over PRIOR same-kind days, excluding 15/11 (a documented non-recurrent event). Minimum history is ≥ 2 such days; otherwise there is no forecast and d = p. Under this rule, 14/11 uses 12-13, and 15/11 and 16/11 use 12-14; 17/11 and 18/11 get no forecast. The rule needs no H and has no tuned parameter. Zero-run sensitivities, which are not decision rules: the leave-one-out pool, a pool that keeps 15/11, two-sided (no floor), a mean-of-normalised-shape aggregator, and single-source-day forecasts as a dose-response. SECONDARY closed loop, gated (F2/F3): v1.4 continuous anchored ratio with D = 900 s fixed a priori (the dev median first-drop horizon of 727-799 s rounded up to one bin) and U = 300 s. v1.3 per-bin K=2 is retired as a design iteration and reported as a mechanism finding.
revisedDecisions.rationale: (1) It is the only variant with evidence of improving both lateness and the thesis's own visible-change metric while leaving the served set identical. On the v1.3 smoke cell: late 7 -> 0, visible60 0.080 -> 0.023, served 87 = 87. v1.3 on the same cell gave visible60 0.224 and served 85. (2) A per-trip stretch is what option (a), a time-dependent ETA, would compute, but without a core change. Industry also keeps ETA layers separate from dispatch. (3) The causal pool removes the leakage attack at no cost: calibration late60 0.19% causal vs 0.34% leave-one-out. (4) The floor follows the a priori asymmetric-loss evidence. revisedDecisions.choice: Two instruments, with no tuned parameter in the primary one. (i) PRIMARY, a promise-layer (display) forecast scored by exact offline replay. For each served rider: t0 = publishedAtMs of the drop initialPromise, P0 = its p, D = P0 - t0. P_F = max(P0, S(t0, D)), where S solves integral_{t0}^{S} 1/g(s) ds = D. g = 1 inside the current bin (anchored on the measured current level), g = m(b(s))/m(b(t0)) in later bins, held from bin 8 as the world does. The same stretch applies to the pickup promise and to every later revision at its own publishedAtMs. No H is needed. (ii) SECONDARY, closed loop: v1.4 (forecast-v2) with D = 900 s fixed a priori and U = 300 s as built, plus a one-sided floor r = max(1, r). The floor is a small wrapper change and must pass the existing tests, new floor tests and the mutants before sealing. v1.3 is retired for test use, and the D = 1800 dev run is diagnostic only. Sources for both: CAUSAL past same-kind days with 15-min factors. 15/11 is excluded a priori as a documented incident day, since 'anticipated' means a regular pattern. A day with no such past day (17/11, and 12/11 in dev) gets no forecast. Weekday test pools: 14/11 <- {12,13}; 15/11 and 16/11 <- {12,13,14}; 18/11 <- {17}. Aggregator: the implemented mean of absolute profiles. Zero-run sensitivities, not decision rules: LOO-no15, two-sided, 15/11 included, 12/11 excluded (possible holiday, unverified), and the crude per-bin stretch.
revisedDecisions.rationale: Within a bin the true path is flat, so a per-rider stretch is the exact time-dependent ETA. It removes the within-bin over-padding that made v1.3 oscillate, and it has no free parameter, so it cannot be blamed on tuning. The causal pool removes the leakage objection at almost no cost. Computed from source days only, it gives floored v1.4 r(t) tables nearly identical to LOO-no15 on weekday mornings: max r on 14/11 w07 1.0766 vs 1.0695, on 15/11 1.0871 vs 1.0794, and identical on 16/11. The floor follows a priori from the asymmetric loss in the business sources, not from calibration results. D = 900 is the median first-drop horizon on task-B (about 727 s) rounded up to the bin length. Under v1.4, r(t) is 1 at the bin start and approaches g at the bin end, which matches the share of a ~13-min trip that falls into later bins.

revisedDecisions.choice: Two families, each with FWER <= 0.05. FAMILY A (display layer, C-30, 34 cells, sealed as a pre-registered measurement). Y1_c = share of served riders with A - P_F > 60 s; E60_c = share with A - P_F < -60 s; the arm value is the unweighted mean over cells. Inference: a stratified cluster bootstrap that resamples day-windows within each window stratum, with stratum weights 9/34, 14/34 and 11/34, B = 10,000, a new sealed seed and 95% percentile intervals. The fixed sequence runs A1 -> A2 -> A3. A1: Delta Y1 (F - naive) has UB95 < 0, point <= -1.0 pp, and point Delta E60 <= +1.0 pp; it earns the 'strong' label if UB95 < -1.0 pp. A2: Y1(F) - Y1(flat pad) has UB95 < 0, where the pad is P0 + k*D and k = sum(P_F - P0)/sum(D) over all test C-30 riders, computed from promises only. A3: the same test against a per-window pad k_w matched in price per window, i.e. information versus a rush-hour rule of thumb. Pre-declared downgrades: a leave-one-day-out estimate >= 0 gives 'driven by one day'; a cluster-t interval (df = 12) with UB >= 0 gives 'fragile to small-cluster inference'. The cell bootstrap is also reported for continuity with T3.8. FAMILY B (closed loop, cells actually run, paired with the same-clock naive run). With 6-8 clusters, inference uses a cluster-level t interval on paired cluster means (df = G - 1); the stratified cluster bootstrap is also reported. Two chains, each at two-sided alpha = 0.025 (Bonferroni). Chain M: B1, Mplus-30F - Mplus-30 forced share (M5_nonNormalShare) has UB < 0 and a relative point reduction >= 30%, then B2, own-break share (A > own first promise + 30 s) has UB < 0. Chain C: B3, C-30F - C-30 served has LB >= -2 riders per cell (the T3.9 margin); then B4, visible60 has UB <= +2.5 pp; then B5, late60 against its own first promise has UB < 0. Claims: 'forecast-aware promising removes the anticipable part of lateness' needs A1. 'Better than padding' needs A2 as well. 'Integrating it into the Runner is safe for service and stability' needs B3 and B4. 'The deadline rule's forced decisions were largely an artefact of naive promises' needs B1. Windows, other arms, snow and everything else are descriptive.
revisedDecisions.rationale: Day-windows are the units that carry independent traffic information; windows are fixed design strata. Stratified cluster resampling respects both and avoids the morning-free resamples that would sink an unstratified test. The display family is a measurement with a near-certain sign, so its informative tests are the padding comparisons. The closed-loop family holds the real uncertainty, and with few clusters a t-based interval is more honest than a degenerate percentile bootstrap. Splitting the closed-loop chains means a failure on C-30 service cannot silence the Mplus question, and the reverse.

critiques.problem: The primary hypothesis H-F1 is run through v1.3, which has a static-matrix defect. The repository already documents it on the very dev cell the methodologist's design uses. On d20181112-s10-r1-w07, v1.3 K=2 eliminates lateness (7 late riders to 0) but raises visible60 from 0.080 to 0.224. It also raises earlier drop revisions from 187.5 s to 1748.1 s and cuts served riders from 87 to 85 (smoke-breakdown-2026-10-06.txt; EVIDENCE-ADDENDUM-1 'root cause: vehicles run ahead of the plan'). I applied the zero-run time-dependent display layer to the naive v1.2 run of the same cell, with the same source days (13-16/11). It gives late>60 s 7 to 0, visible60 0.080 to 0.023 and served 87 (read-only, this session, unsaved). So the closed loop bundles the forecast's benefit with churn the implementation causes itself. A reviewer would read 'forecast-aware promising worsens stability', and that is an artefact of a uniform static inflation. The methodologist also declines to predict the direction of visible60, although the only dev evidence shows a 2.8x increase.

The rationale says 'Updating once per bin keeps promise revisions at bin boundaries only, as in v1.2, so no extra visible jitter'. The repo's own per-bin K=2 smoke contradicts this: visible60 goes from 0.080 to 0.224, earlier revisions from 187.5 s to 1748.1 s, and served from 87 to 85 (smoke-breakdown-2026-10-06.txt line 2; compare-v13-control-2026-10-06.txt: 423 decision digests differ). Revisions happen at every re-projection, because vehicles drive measured times while the Runner expects r times measured. The practitioner's primary E1/N1 inherits this unacknowledged cost.

A stratified cell bootstrap treats cells in the same day-window as independent. They share an identical factor path. In w07, the intra-day correlation of C-30 late60 is about 0.92 (one-way ANOVA ICC, rider-experience-2026-10-05-cells.tsv: 14/11 0.170, 0.113; 15/11 0.227, 0.207, 0.222; 16/11 0.045, 0.097, 0.074; 17/11 0.015). So w07 carries about 4 independent mornings, not 9 cells. The power simulation draws independent N(0, sigma) noise per cell, so it overstates power. The leave-one-day-out downgrade rule helps but does not replace cluster inference.

An unstratified cell bootstrap on 21 weekday cells hides that there are only 8 weekday day-windows (w07: 14, 15, 16; w08: 14, 15, 16; w17: 14, 16), and the w07 signal comes from 3 days. The same ICC of about 0.92 applies. The 95% intervals will be far too narrow.

The methodologist's own numbers show that the snow cells test nothing new. The world anchors at the window start and reproduces only the ramp inside the window. From the factor files, 15/11 14-16 ends at 1.403 and 15-17 at 1.460, with mean K=2 growth 1.0218 and 1.0244. Every weekday 07-09 morning is steeper: end ratio 1.469-1.656, K=2 growth 1.0248-1.0330 (read-only computation this session; consistent with day-profiles-2026-10-06.txt). The forecast r on that afternoon is about 1, so C-30F equals naive there. The result is a naive run under a milder-than-normal ramp, which the existing naive w07 test runs already show (C-30 late60 13.0%). Also, '5/8 built' is outdated: normalize-snow-2026-10-06.out lists 8/8 'ok with label base'.

16 runs (C-30-F and Mplus-30-F on 8 snow cells) are spent on a ramp milder than an ordinary weekday morning, as shown above, with r_b 1.000-1.005 after the floor. P9, 'snow late60 at least 2x weekday-w07 C-30-F', mostly restates that a forecast cannot anticipate what it does not see. It is predictable without running.

The primary forecast uses future days of the same week (16/11 forecasts 14/11 and 15/11; 17/11 is forecast from 18/11) and is symmetric. Neither choice buys accuracy: the methodologist's own calibration MAE is 12.8 s past-only vs 13.2 s LOO-no15. The symmetric version knowingly carries harm. Causal K=2 r on weekday 17-19 is 0.976-1.008 (my computation from preflight_world_v1_3.ratio), so the primary pools a predicted w17 harm (their P3) with the w07 benefit. They then spend 11 x 2 runs to measure a harm that the asymmetric-loss rule in SOURCES-2026-10-05.md would avoid.

The primary efficacy tests are all but certain to pass, and their outcome is effectively previewed. Calibration cells share days, and therefore factor paths, with the test cells (split-t38-v1.json: calibration 14/11 r1-r2, 15/11 r3, 16/11 r3 in w07). On those calibration cells, the causal display forecast already takes C-30 w07 late60 from 17.66% to 0.00% (this session, unsaved). With an ICC of about 0.92, the test-cell result is largely known. Labelling H-F1/E1 'confirmatory' overstates the evidence. They should be called pre-registered measurements, and inferential weight should go to the genuinely open question: whether Mplus-30's forced share survives a forecast.

'H = 2 x (7.5 min + 727 s / 2)' is ad hoc arithmetic that lands near 30 min. It is not a derivation. The methodologist's version (r is about 1 + (g - 1)/2 for a 13-min horizon) is cleaner. The integral version for D = 13 min with a uniform offset gives about 0.43 (g - 1) (my estimate), so K=2 is defensible, but the formula should not be presented as a priori.

The C-30F v1.3 smoke on a task-B cell already exists and passed (C:/RideBoundData/research/tier3-forecast-checks-v1/smoke-k2; compare-v13-control-2026-10-06.txt). Re-running 4 C-30-F dev cells duplicates it. Only an Mplus-30F smoke is missing.

With a per-bin refresh, H = 15 min means K=1, and preflight_world_v1_3.ratio returns exactly 1.0 ('K = 1 gives r = 1 exactly', module docstring). My dispatch-integrated arm would have been identical to naive. I took my offline 'uniform H=15' numbers from continuous t, which v1.3 does not implement.

The current bin uses the measured speed (g = 1). Later bins use the anchored forecast growth m(b)/m(b0), held from bin 8 on. The displayed drop time is D = max(p, stretch(pub, p - pub)), recomputed at every Runner revision. No H is needed, because each rider's own horizon is integrated. Sources are causal: only PRIOR same-kind days, with a minimum-history rule of at least 2 prior days, otherwise no forecast (D = p). Weekdays: 14/11 uses 12-13, 15/11 uses 12-14, 16/11 uses 12-15. Weekends 17-18/11 get no forecast. Leave-one-out sources (with and without 15/11) are a zero-run sensitivity. The r-table goes into the sealed plan. Causal r on the run cells is 1.000-1.065 (w07) and 0.988-1.026 (w08), so no clamp code is needed. No tuning on test.
revisedDecisions.rationale: (1) The display layer is the faithful time-dependent (piecewise-speed) promise model that addendum 2 rates as a large core change. It is applied only to the promise channel, which needs no core change. (2) On the same dev cell and source days it dominates v1.3: same lateness removal, about 10x less churn, no served loss. (3) It is exact in this world: for riders with dispatch part 0, |A - stretch along the true path| <= 1.00 s for 658/660 dev riders (validate-stretch-2026-10-06.txt), so dwell scaling is not a material approximation. (4) Causal sources cost nothing in accuracy (methodologist's past-only MAE 12.8 vs 13.2 s) and remove the leakage objection. (5) The minimum-history rule is a priori (one day is not a profile), and the only weekend-source evidence shows harm. (6) v1.3 is kept unchanged because it is tested (23/23 checks, 8/8 mutants) and its forecast-off mode reproduces v1.2 exactly. v1.4 costs about 1.5x disk per run and changes the naive comparator (v1.4 naive: 5 late vs v1.2: 7).

PRIMARY instrument: a promise-layer display. Every pickup/drop promise and every revision, published at t with Runner ETA p, is shown as D = max(p, S(t, p - t)). S is promise_stretch.stretch with forecast_weight: g = 1 in the current bin and m(b)/m(b0) in later bins. No H is needed, because each rider's own horizon is integrated.

SECONDARY instrument: closed loop with v1.3 UNCHANGED (forecast-v1), K = 2 (H = 30 min at per-bin refresh), same causal-no15 source lists.
- K is fixed a priori: K = 1 is identically 1 (verified, ratio() line 86-87). For the ~727-s median dev horizon promised at a uniformly random point in a bin, r ≈ 1 + ½(g-1).

- The 34-cell deployment mean is co-reported; the weekend difference is 0 by construction.

Development: task-B (12-13/11 w07) only, the only day-disjoint set.
- The 15 calibration cells share 12 of 13 test day-windows (ICC of C-30 w07 late60 = 0.917, verified), so they are used for NO choice.
- Every earlier look at them (by all three debaters) is disclosed as a preview.

Closed loop: the 16 weekday w07 and w08 test cells, 6 day-windows.
- Weekday w17 is excluded on input grounds: causal r there is 0.976-1.005, so a one-sided rule would be r = 1, identical to naive.
- Weekends are excluded: no forecast.

Equivalence and gates, run BEFORE any test job:
- S1, Mplus-30F smoke on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 with the existing forecast-check-k2.json. Implementation check only; its outcomes are never used.
- E1, Mplus-30 v1.3 forecast-off on one weekday w08 test cell drawn with the sealed seed, ORIGINAL label, new output root.
- E2, C-30 v1.3 forecast-on K = 1 sham (causal-no15 sources) on one weekday w07 test cell drawn with the sealed seed, original label.
- Each is compared with its T3.8 run on: decisions with times, signed v/e/p table, served set, alight times, and frames after stripping run-salted fields.
- Positive control at zero runs: the comparator must flag U vs C-30 on the same cell.
- Any failure halts Family B. Pre-declared fallback: fresh v1.3-off naive comparators for the 8 weekday w07 cells only (16 runs), and Family B is restricted to w07.

Snow: optional tier 4, C-30 naive (v1.3 forecast-off) x all 8 built cells, with display replay. Descriptive and framed as an 'unanticipated ordinary-size ramp' (a negative control), not a stress test.
decisions.rationale:
Day-windows are the units of independent traffic information: ICC 0.92, and the 3 cells of 15/11 w07 have late60 0.227/0.207/0.222. Windows are fixed design strata.

The active-population rule follows from the sealed forecast policy, not from outcomes. Weekend cells, where the policy is off, contribute an exact zero.

Closed-loop cells are where the forecast is non-trivial and where M+ forcing lives.

E1 tests the Mplus gate path and environment stability. RideBound-deadline HEAD is 1ce15e9, dated 2026-09-25, i.e. before T3.8. E2 isolates the snapshot-patch path from the r effect (ms rounding). The existing control-off run already showed 718/718 identical decisions for C-30.

Snow:
- Verified 8/8 cells 'ok with label base' (normalize-snow-2026-10-06.out).
- The world anchors at the window start, so the storm's absolute level is absent.
- The in-window ramp (end ratio 1.403/1.460) is milder than weekday mornings (1.469-1.656), and the causal forecast is flat.
- It therefore adds only a ledger illustration, hence the optional tier.
decisions.dissent: Methodologist: the primary should be the 34-cell zero-filled estimand over 13 day-windows, which blocks any 'chosen windows' charge. Practitioner: naive snow runs belong in tier 1, because they supply the 'unanticipated' half of the accountability ledger that the business case rests on.

decisions.fork: F4 Primary outcomes and decision rules
decisions.decision:
Family A (display, C-30, 21 weekday cells; fixed sequence) is primary. Family B (closed loop, 16 cells) is secondary: one classification chain and one non-inferiority chain, each at alpha 0.025, plus a pre-declared deployment rule.

Inference:
- Interval of record: stratified day-window cluster bootstrap.
- Downgrade checks: leave-one-day-out and cluster-t.
- The cell bootstrap is reported for continuity only.

The full rule is in primaryRule.
decisions.rationale:
Lateness against the first shown drop time is the quantity the Via, delivery and paratransit sources price. Churn is the thesis's own UX metric and was the closed loop's failure mode, so it is a sealed guard.

The display outcome is largely previewed: calibration cells share day-windows, and the predictability table has been seen. Family A is therefore labelled a pre-registered measurement, and its genuinely informative step is A3, information vs an equal-price buffer. Dev evidence for A3 (task-B, unsaved): pad 1.80% vs forecast 0.00%.

Stratified cluster resampling avoids the morning-free resamples that sink an unstratified 13-cluster bootstrap (verified: (10/13)^13 = 0.033 > 0.025). Family B carries the real uncertainty, so it gets a classification for the open M+ question instead of a pass/fail. Price is reported, not gated, because no anchored tolerability threshold exists. Earliness is the only over-quoting gate.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic and methodologist: with only 8 clusters (2-3 per stratum), percentile intervals from a stratified cluster bootstrap are coarse and can be anti-conservative. A per-day-window sign count in EVERY active day-window (not just w07), or a cluster-t interval, should be the decisive criterion rather than a downgrade label.

decisions.fork: F5 Secondary and descriptive outcomes
decisions.decision:
All outcomes are paired, descriptive and use the Family A bootstrap.

(1) Price riders see: first drop and first pickup extension (mean, p50, p90; seconds and % of horizon) by window. The demand effect uses the Lyft elasticity -0.0427 applied to the PICKUP extension only, labelled an extrapolation. Also report the count of displayed pickups beyond request + 600 s, an operational inconsistency because feasibility stays naive.

(2) Accuracy: lateness CDF, signed bias, MAE (comparable to Via's 24.24 s), late30/120/300, early60, late pickup > 60 s.

(3) Displayed stability: visible60 and visible120, jump share, and S_j on the displayed sequence. The T3.8 conformal gamma is recomputed on displayed promises with the same alpha and split. No recalibration runs.

(4) Three-way ledger per late rider against the naive first promise: dispatch part Σ(p - e); anticipated traffic (D0 - P0); unanticipated remainder (A - D0 - dispatch). Cell-level shares map to 49 CFR 37.131(f)(3)(ii) and App. D.

(5) The {U, C-30} x {naive, display} factorial, plus display for Mplus-30, Mplus-60 and V-30.

(6) Closed loop:
- served, wait, ride and door-to-door;
- common-rider late60, forced share, own-break, non-normal count;
- earlier/later revision seconds;
- C-30F vs Mplus-30F served (H2a replication, ±2) and action-sequence agreement;
- r-lines checked against the sealed table.

(7) Sensitivities from F1, plus the citywide pad, an additive pad, and an empirical per-bin pad learned from task-B lateness.

(8) Optional tiers: snow late60/late300, the unanticipated share and the ledger; noise world, the share of the display benefit that survives.

(9) Money ($5 Via, $10 Access-A-Ride): labelled illustrative, shown next to the scale gap (late300 = 0 under the capped rules; field thresholds are 10-15 min).
decisions.rationale: Every gain must sit next to its price in seconds and in riders. The ledger turns the forecast into the 'anticipated' baseline that the regulation refers to. That is the practical tool for a contract manager. The factorial is the operator's 'do I need both?' answer, and it costs zero runs. Recomputing gamma tests whether the T3.8 margin, set by one 07-09 cell, was mostly anticipable traffic.
decisions.dissent: Methodologist: under any forecast the ledger identity's residual (alight - last promise) is no longer zero. Splitting 'unanticipated' from forecast error at execution therefore needs the identity re-verified per rider, or the ledger shares are not interpretable. The skeptic adds that money translations should be omitted entirely given the scale gap.

decisions.fork: F6 Predictions to seal
decisions.decision: Seal predictions PA1-PA9 (display), PB1-PB8 (closed loop), PC1 (controls) and the optional PS1/PN1 exactly as listed in predictions. Make no prediction for the dev smoke outcomes or for Branch selection. Disclose that the display predictions are not blind: test-day forecast error and calibration previews were seen. The closed-loop and optional predictions are the ones that can genuinely fail.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic: the display predictions PA1-PA6 are near-certain given the calibration previews and should carry no evidential weight in the write-up. Practitioner: PB1 has no offline proxy for forcing, so its interval is a guess.

decisions.fork: F7 Threats to validity and mitigations
decisions.decision:
Threats, each with its mitigation:

(1) Near-tautology: a uniform citywide factor on a 96-node OD closure, with world and forecast from the same factor source. Mitigation: frame the result as the measured anticipable share and an upper bound for a time-of-day ratio forecast; report forecast error per day-window; make no real-world effect-size claim; run the optional noise tier.

(2) Previewed test: calibration shares day-windows with test (ICC 0.92), and the predictability table has been seen. Mitigation: Family A labelled 'pre-registered measurement'; dev = task-B only; disclose every pre-seal look, including the debaters' unsaved calibration computations and the input-only r-tables in this ruling.

(3) Thin, odd history: 14/11 rests on 12-13/11; 12/11 is possibly the Veterans Day observance (unverified; its 08:00 factor is 2.797 vs 3.34-3.54); one week only. Mitigation: LOO and 12/11-excluded sensitivities; the claim is conditional on this week.

(4) Few clusters (3 weekday mornings). Mitigation: stratified cluster bootstrap, sign counts, leave-one-day-out and cluster-t downgrades.

(5) Reuse of naive runs across code versions. Mitigation: E1/E2 with a positive control, and the fallback rule.

(6) Static-matrix artefact in the closed loop. Mitigation: closed loop is secondary; churn is reported as a static-matrix integration cost, with v1.4 dev showing partial mitigation (0.167 vs 0.224); no claim that forecasting harms stability in general.

(7) Changed served sets (closed loop). Mitigation: B-C1, common-rider late60.

(8) Display assumptions: riders do not react (no cancellations in the sim); the Runner ledger records Runner promises; pickup feasibility stays naive; dwell is stretched. Mitigation: state all of them; count pickups displayed outside the window; check the oracle residual on test (PA8).

(9) Analyst degrees of freedom: one-sided rule, causal pool, 15/11 exclusion, minimum history, visibleD60 metric. Mitigation: list each in the seal with its a priori reason, run a sensitivity for each, and disclose that they were settled after dev looks.

(10) Snow: completed-trip demand, still 108 requests per cell, absolute level removed, one afternoon, overlapping windows. Mitigation: descriptive only, optional.

(11) Scale gap of 60 s vs 10-15 min penalties. Mitigation: claim ETA reliability, not money.

(12) Volatile disk: C: free was ~57,240 MiB this morning and 65,298 MiB at my check. Mitigation: a per-job live gate against GiB floors, seeded order within tiers, so any truncation leaves a random subset.

(13) Evidence-pack errata: the largest 15-min step per day is 5.1-16.2%, not 10.6-16.2% (verified); the snow cells are 8/8 built.

(14) Number provenance. Mitigation: every dev number is regenerated by saved, hashed scripts before the seal; independent re-analysis agent plus a number-tracing reviewer, as in T3.8.
decisions.rationale: These are the routes by which a hostile examiner would attribute the result to tuning, selection, leakage, artefact or circularity. Each is answered by a pre-declared rule, a zero-run analysis or narrower wording.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic: the noise robustness test should be core, not optional, because it is the only direct answer to the tautology attack. Methodologist: W4 noise parameters are uncalibrated (sigma 0.08, rho 0.7, shockRate 0.02), so any noise result is conditional on an arbitrary magnitude.

decisions.fork: F8 Direction check
decisions.rationale:
After the C-30 gate, the remaining failure is morning-ramp lateness: weekday w07 14.44%, the caps barely help, and it is traffic-caused (contract-split-check). Dev evidence shows a promise-layer forecast removes it, and also displayed churn, at about 21 s on a ~13-min quote, while dispatch is untouched. That maps onto deployed ETA layers and onto the 'anticipated' test in 49 CFR 37.131(f)(3)(ii) and App. D. This is a measured effect plus a tool, with no novelty claim.

Runs are spent only where replay cannot answer. The closed-loop M+ question protects the thesis against its most obvious examiner attack, whichever way it comes out.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic, hostile-examiner view: in this world the display result is a closed-form consequence of the factor files. Its research value is small, and the best use of the remaining ~5 weeks is to write up T3.8/T3.9 now, with only the 32-run M+ question as new evidence.

result.primaryRule:
FAMILY A (PRIMARY; zero-run display replay; arm C-30)

Population: the 21 weekday T3.8 test cells. These form 8 day-windows in 3 window strata: w07 {14,15,16}/11, w08 {14,15,16}/11, w17 {14,16}/11.

Per served rider r:
- t0 = publishedAtMs of the drop initialPromise; P0 = its p.
- A = simTime of the first passengerAlighted.
- Displayed first drop D0 = max(P0, S(t0, P0 - t0)), where S = promise_stretch.stretch with forecast_weight(m, t0) and m = the causal-no15 profile (14/11 <- 12,13; 15/11 and 16/11 <- 12,13,14). Every later drop revision is displayed the same way at its own publishedAtMs.

Cell metrics:
- Y = share of served riders with A - D0 > 60 s. The naive value Y_n is late_drop60 of t38_rider_experience.py (A - P0 > 60 s).
- E = share of served riders with A - D0 < -60 s.
- Vis = share of promised riders whose Σ|D_i - D_{i-1}| over non-closed drop revisions exceeds 60 s. The naive value is visible60.

Estimand: the unweighted mean over the 21 cells of the per-cell paired differences.

Interval of record: stratified day-window cluster bootstrap.
- Within each stratum, resample its day-windows with replacement, pool their cells, and take the cell mean.
- Combine strata with weights 8/21, 8/21 and 5/21.
- B = 10,000, random.Random(20261007), 95% percentile interval = sorted indices 249 and 9750.

Fixed sequence (each step is tested only if the previous one passes):
- A1 (accuracy): passes iff ALL of:
  - point ΔY ≤ -2.0 pp;
  - UB95(ΔY) < 0;
  - ΔY < 0 in each of the 3 weekday-w07 day-windows;
  - point ΔE ≤ +1.0 pp.
- A2 (churn guard): passes iff UB95(ΔVis) ≤ +1.0 pp.
- A3 (information vs buffer): passes iff UB95[Y(display) - Y(pad_w)] < 0.
  - pad_w shows P0 + k_w·(P0 - t0), and each revision p_i + k_w·(P0 - t0).
  - k_w = Σ(D0 - P0) / Σ(P0 - t0) over all weekday C-30 test riders of window w.
  - k_w is computed from promises only; the script must assert that it reads no alight time.

Claims:
- A1: 'a forecast-aware display removes most anticipable lateness at the measured price'.
- A1 + A2: '... without adding displayed churn'.
- A1 + A2 + A3: '... because of time-of-day information, beyond an equal-price rush-hour buffer'.

Labels and downgrades:
- Every Family A result is labelled 'pre-registered measurement on day-windows previewed by calibration cells'.
- If any leave-one-day-out (drop 14, 15 or 16/11) point ΔY ≥ 0, the label is 'driven by one day'.
- If a stratified cluster-t interval (df = 8 - 3 = 5) has UB ≥ 0, the label is 'fragile to small-cluster inference'.
- The T3.8-style cell bootstrap and the 34-cell deployment mean (weekend Δ = 0 by construction) are co-reported.

FAMILY B (SECONDARY; closed loop)

Setup:
- v1.3 unchanged, K = 2, causal-no15 sources.
- The 16 weekday w07/w08 test cells, 6 day-windows.
- Paired with the reused T3.8 naive runs, valid only if E1 and E2 pass.
- Same stratified cluster bootstrap with 2 strata of 3, B = 10,000, the same seed, 97.5% intervals = indices 124 and 9875.
- Two chains at alpha 0.025 each.

Chain M (classification of Mplus-30F - Mplus-30 forced share, M5_nonNormalShare):
- ARTEFACT iff the relative reduction is ≥ 50%, AND it decreases in 6/6 day-windows, AND UB97.5 < 0.
- PARTIAL iff the relative reduction is ≥ 25% and UB97.5 < 0, but it is not ARTEFACT.
- INCONCLUSIVE iff the relative reduction is ≥ 25% and UB97.5 ≥ 0.
- PERSISTS iff the relative reduction is < 25%.
- Own-break (A > own first promise + 30 s) is classified the same way.

Chain C:
- B-C1 passes iff LB97.5[served(C-30F) - served(C-30)] ≥ -2 riders per cell (the T3.9 margin).
- Deployment rule: recommend integrating the forecast into the Runner only if ALL of:
  - B-C1 passes;
  - visible60(C-30F) ≤ Vis(C-30 display) + 1.0 pp, over the same 16 cells (point);
  - late60(C-30F vs its own first promise) ≤ Y(C-30 display) + 1.0 pp (point).
- Otherwise, recommend the display layer.

Everything else (windows, other arms, the optional tiers) is descriptive, with CIs and no significance language.

result.runPlan:
All runs use v1.3, unchanged, from E:\Code\RideBound-deadline. Outputs go to a new root on C: (e.g. C:\RideBoundData\research\tier3-forecast-v1), using the original T3.8 labels.

Tier 0, gates (3 runs). Run before any test job:
- S1: Mplus-30F smoke on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 with the existing forecast-check-k2.json. Implementation check only.
- E1: Mplus-30, forecast off, on one seeded weekday-w08 test cell.
- E2: C-30, K = 1 sham (causal-no15 sources), on one seeded weekday-w07 test cell.
- Halt Family B if E1 or E2 fails. The fallback is then 16 fresh v1.3-off naive runs (C-30 and Mplus-30 x 8 weekday-w07 cells), Family B restricted to w07, and tier 2 dropped.

Tier 1 (16 runs): C-30F and Mplus-30F on the 8 weekday-w07 test cells: 14/11 r3, r4; 15/11 r1, r2, r4; 16/11 r1, r2, r4. Sealed r-table, seeded order.

Tier 2 (16 runs): C-30F and Mplus-30F on the 8 weekday-w08 test cells (same days and samples).

Reserve: ≤ 3 one-time infrastructure reruns.

Committed total: 35 + 3 = 38 new runs, about 3.0 GiB at the measured 77-80 MiB per v1.3 run.

Tier 3, optional (9 runs; only if the live gate allows after tier 2): noise robustness.
- 1 smoke: C-30 naive on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 in a measured-base x W4-noise world. Verifies that v1.3 accepts sigma > 0 with a measured base (unverified).
- Then C-30 naive on the 8 weekday-w07 test cells in that world, scored offline by the display layer.

Tier 4, optional (8 runs): C-30 naive, v1.3 forecast-off, on all 8 snow cells (15/11 w14 and w15, r1-r4). Descriptive, with display replay.

Maximum: 55 + 3 = 58 new runs, about 4.6 GiB, plus the 5 dev runs already used (516 MiB measured). That is well inside the ~6,000 MiB headroom over a 51,200 MiB floor on C:. E: is not used unless the owner permits.

Disk gate per job: start only if C: free - 51,200 MiB ≥ 410 MiB, read live with Get-PSDrive. C: read 65,298 MiB now vs ~57,240 MiB this morning, so it is volatile. If the gate fails, stop and list unrun jobs in the sealed order.

Zero-run work:
- display replay on the 170 T3.8 test runs (5 arms x 34 cells);
- display replay on task-B dev (all arms) and the 15 calibration runs (descriptive, flagged);
- pads, factorial, ledger and sensitivities.

Wall time: about 38-58 runs x ~200 s effective at 6 workers ≈ 2.1-3.2 h, on AC power.
implementationChecks: Before the seal, regenerate every dev number cited in the plan from saved, hashed scripts, with output files opened in mode 'x'. This covers: task-B display (C-30, Mplus-30, U; LOO-no15 and causal), pads, extension, visibleD60, the causal-no15 K=2 r-tables for the 6 closed-loop day-windows, and the input-only snow and weekday growth ratios. No forecast outcome may be computed on any test cell before the seal; calibration cells are not recomputed.
Pad comparator code asserts that it reads promises only (no alight times) when computing k_w. k_w values are written to a file before any outcome metric is computed.

Dry-run the full analysis pipeline (Family A and B tables, stratified cluster bootstrap, cluster-t, leave-one-day-out, sign counts) on task-B dev data before the seal. Unit-test the stratified cluster bootstrap on a synthetic case with a known answer.

Equivalence comparator: compares decisions with times, signed v/e/p table, served set, alight times and frames after stripping runId/publicationId(s)/*Hash. Positive control: U vs C-30 on the same cell must differ. Mutation test: perturb one decision time and one alight time; both must be detected. E1 and E2 must pass before any tier-1 job; the halt and fallback rules are sealed.
